ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: $ABCD$ is a square 4 inches on a side, and each of the inside squares is formed by joining the midpoints of the outer square's sides. What is the area of the shaded region in square inches? <image1>
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an outer square ABCD, with A, B, C, D respectively marked near the four corners. Inside the outer square there is a tilted square, in the shape of a rhombus, and its four vertices respectively fall at the midpoints of the four sides of the outer square. Inside this tilted square there is also a smaller upright white square, and its four vertices fall at the midpoints of the sides of the tilted square. The gray shaded part is exactly the region inside the tilted square and outside the small white square. Reasoning: The side length of the outer square ABCD is 4 inches, so the area is 4×4=16 square inches. The area of a new square formed by connecting the midpoints of the four sides of a square is half the area of the original square, therefore the area of the tilted inner square is 16÷2=8 square inches. The smaller white square is also formed by connecting the midpoints of the sides of the tilted square, so the area is 8÷2=4 square inches. Shaded area = area of the tilted square − area of the small white square = 8−4=4 square inches.

method.method_draft: Use successive midpoint-square area halving. From the image, identify the outer square ABCD, the large tilted inner square whose vertices lie at the midpoints of ABCD's sides, and the smaller upright white square whose vertices lie at the midpoints of the tilted square's sides. The shaded region is exactly the area inside the tilted square but outside the smaller upright square. From the text, the outer square has side length 4, so its area is 16. A square formed by joining side midpoints has half the area of the original square; therefore the tilted square has area 8 and the smaller upright square has area 4. Subtract to get shaded area 8 - 4 = 4.

method.method_draft: Dissect the shaded region into four congruent triangles. From the image, the gray region consists of the top, right, bottom, and left triangular parts between the tilted diamond and the central upright square. From the text, ABCD has side 4, so the midpoints of its sides are 2 inches from adjacent corners. The diamond's side-midpoints form the central upright square whose vertices are halfway along the diamond sides; equivalently its side length is 2, and each shaded triangular piece has base 2 along one side of the central square and perpendicular height 1 to the corresponding vertex of the diamond. Each triangle has area (1/2)(2)(1)=1, and there are four such triangles, so the shaded area is 4.
